newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court sets aside GM Hughes patent ruling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court sets aside GM Hughes patent ruling.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Monday set aside a ruling that the federal government must pay more than $100 million to a unit of General Motors Corp.'s Hughes Electronics Corp. for patent infringement.
At issue in the long-running legal battle dating back to 1973 is a Hughes Aircraft Co. patent for technology that controls the orientation of satellites orbiting the earth.
A federal judge, in a decision affirmed by a U.S. appeals court last year, awarded more than $100 million involving royalties, compensation and interest to Hughes.

But the Justice Department appealed to the Supreme Court, arguing that the appeals court ruling should be set aside in view of a high court decision last month upholding an important, longstanding part of patent law.
The Supreme Court, in a brief order, told the appeals court to reconsider its ruling in view of the March decision.
Hughes urged the Supreme Court to reject the appeal, saying the application of the March decision still would yield the same result.
"No purpose would be served by further prolonging this litigation," Hughes said. "This court should deny the government's request to brush away 24 years of litigation and start all over again."
